messages:
incident-bot: [P1 Pager] LATENCY SLO: p99 > 2.5s on runtime-prod (us-west-2). Alerting because streaming stalls and tail latency spiked. Symptoms: p95 up ~800ms, p99 ~2.7s, streaming chunk delays. KV cache eviction rate >> baseline. Paging @maria @sam @jordan. https://alerts.redwood/2001112222

maria: acked. oncall and looking. first pass: is this traffic surge or internal?

sam: i'm looking at cache metrics now — eviction rate has a sharp jump at 14:35 UTC. prefill queue length up 3x.

jordan: saw streaming stalls pop up ~14:36 in traces. chunk_latency shows spikes during prefill windows.

maria: pulling p95/p99 from metrics:
```
query: runtime_latency_seconds{env="prod",region="us-west-2"}
14:30-14:40 p95=750ms p99=2.7s
prefill_task_queue_length{env="prod"} = 420 -> baseline 120
kv_cache_evictions/sec{pool="runtime-prod"} = 620 -> baseline 40
kv_cache_fragmentation_pct{pool="runtime-prod"} = 48% -> baseline 12%
```

sam: wow fragmentation 48% — that's very bad. looks like prefill aggressively populating many small keys, causing eviction churn and more hot misses during decode.

jordan: logs show prefill workers doing many small kv writes tied to long-context sessions. decode path then misses and has to re-prefill which stalls streaming.

ops-bot: action items queued: 1) mitigate customer impact 2) stabilize runtime 3) postmortem.

maria: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle prefill workers for us-west-2 2) temporarily disable prefill on non-critical routes 3) enable route fallback to quantized-smaller model for long-context sessions. Which is fastest?

sam: fastest is throttling prefill. command to taint prefill workers: (run from ops-runbook)
```bash
# set prefill.max_concurrency to 4 for runtime-prod us-west-2
redwoodctl set-config --env prod --region us-west-2 service.prefill.max_concurrency=4
# or disable non-critical prefill routes
redwoodctl set-routing --env prod --region us-west-2 route:long-context:prefill=false
```

maria: i'm applying concurrency cap now. pushing through -- should be quick.

sam: i'm also preparing a temporary compaction job to reduce fragmentation; but compaction is heavy so want to avoid on hot cache. prefer throttling first.

jordan: started enabling route fallback to quantized-small for user-facing chat routes (canary 10%). reduces token decode pressure but may slightly change perf/quality.

maria: concurrency cap applied at 14:40 UTC. observing metrics...

ops-sre: note — informing support to set expectations for customers experiencing streaming stalls.

maria: metrics update 14:45:
```
prefill_task_queue_length -> 160 (was 420)
kv_cache_evictions/sec -> 85 (was 620)
runtime p95 -> 420ms (was 750ms)
runtime p99 -> 1.1s (was 2.7s)
streaming chunk latency tail improved but still some outliers
```

sam: good improvement. still see fragmentation ~40% -> compaction deferred until low traffic window.

jordan: traces show fewer stalls and fewer double-prefill cycles. can keep monitoring for 30m and then revert conservative configs if stable.

maria: next steps:
- Keep prefill.max_concurrency=4 for 1h and monitor
- Schedule fragmentation compaction during 03:00 UTC maintenance window if fragmentation >30%
- Create a follow-up to tune prefill key sizing + batching to reduce small-key churn
- Add eval to catch prefill patterns that cause high fragmentation

sam: i'll open a ticket for model-routing fallback automation so we can more easily shift long-context sessions to heavy-cache-safe variants next time.

jordan: adding a dashboard panel for prefill->decode miss ratio so we can detect this earlier.

maria: handing off to @sam for post-incident monitoring & runbook updates. I'm going to run a quick sanity sweep of related pools and then take a break.

sam: taking over. will keep this channel updated. set next check-in 14:58 UTC.

ops-bot: incident state: mitigated -> partial (customer impact reduced, root cause suspected: prefill-driven kv fragmentation causing eviction churn). Severity remains P1 until stable for 60m.

jordan: note for postmortem: include details on prefill vs decode imbalance, kv key-size distribution, and options considered (throttle prefill, compaction, route fallbacks, scale pool horizontally).

maria: thanks team. if we see any regression re-escalate immediately. :thumbsup:

sam: 15:05 metrics stable; moving to monitoring-only. will keep channel open for 60m then close.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigations applied (prefill throttled, fallback canary enabled). Monitoring.
